used.how: the decision numbers come from the real prompts' chunk 10 in tests/test_moe_exact_replicas.py, not from the A/B's random-token position profile
the streamed side's plan used P.55b's measured pair copy (0.89 ms, both links) as the copy edge, and the result is compared against it
the receivers compute the replica last and wait for the whole copy (moe_exact_model.SUB_TILES 0 in the plan), since a light chip finishes its own experts long before a copy lands
the fill side's serial expert_slot_copy runs once per plan outside the profiled chunk with a sync after it, never in the chunk loop
accuracy compared on re-runs of chunk 10 after a warm re-run, with an off-vs-off repeat that must be bit-identical
the counts are read through flush_counts' [1, 1, 1, slots] buffers (MOE_COUNTS=on) for the plans

contradicted.evidence: its fix line 'split each copy over 2 paths (20.9 / 10.1 ms survive)': P.55c measured the streamed exact split on chunk 10 at +9.2 ms (novel) / +5.1 ms (code) device a chunk vs off; copy layers take 2.10 ms vs the model's 1.21 (results/P.55c_exact_replicas.json, DS41-246)

'P.55a's model at 0.77 ms: novel 8.6, code 2.3 ms a chunk' does not survive in the model: the streamed split measured +9.2 / +5.1 ms; recalibrated at 1.25 ms a copy the model plans 0.77 / 0.06 ms (DS41-246)

missing: the steady path's first re-run of a chunk differs from later re-runs (window carry), so it cannot be an accuracy baseline (DS41-247)
the flat expert orders its experts biggest first (expert_schedule.hpp se_dyn_build), so a receiver's replica would run first unless forced last; the home's hot expert already runs first
the fused head assigns a token's slot in its router rows before any cross-chip count exists, so an on-device exact planner needs a count exchange inside the head or a second head pass (DS41-248)

the exact copy's flag words alternate by the combine's call parity: interleaving exact and stock combine calls on one resources leaves a parity unzeroed (every call must run the exact program while a stream plan is set)

overseer.evidence: no padding or duplicated work: the replica is the spare slot P.46 already allocates; the kernels were extended (router_rows.hpp uneven split, fx_wait.hpp) instead
no Python-built op added or touched; the changes are in the C++ fork's kernels and host program (routed_experts_combine, flat_routed_expert, fused head kernel)
no fork regression or unit suite run on the 8x4; only the model-level test (test_moe_exact_replicas) and the gate's units

(2) two paths a copy: P.55b's both-links jobs used as built; (3) the home re-reads the slot from DRAM (P.55b's port reads; the home already computes its hot expert first: the flat expert's biggest-first order); (1) partly: the receivers wait for the whole copy (one token a call), not block by block - per block would save at most the replica's own compute (~0.05-0.1 ms) of a 0.9 ms gap. Copies on time at the measured copy time (P.55a's model, whole-copy wait): 0.89 ms novel 2 of 289 / 5.49 ms, code 0 of 66 / 1.13 ms; 1.25 ms novel 0 of 44 / 0.77 ms, code 0 of 4 / 0.06 ms

(1) test_moe_exact_replicas records exact_device_ms_{off,fill,exact}_{novel,code} and exact_experts_ms_* at chunk 10 after the device's own prefill: novel 185.9 / 161.5 / 195.0, code 170.5 / 158.3 / 175.6 (experts 56.5 / 39.2 / 68.7 and 46.5 / 38.9 / 51.7); (2) receivers compute the replica last (expert_schedule.hpp SE_FX_SPARE) and read it once the copy landed (fx_wait.hpp; whole copy, see OV-39); (3) a copy layer takes +1.0-1.2 ms over the same split with the copies in place (novel 23 layers 2.10 vs 0.93 ms, code 8 layers 1.98 vs 0.96); (4) every side bit-identical to off on every MoE layer, the repeats bit-identical, spare slots spoiled first
